messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test case `test_getShortClassName_Class()` asserts that the short class name for `String[].class` should be "String[]". However, the current implementation of `ClassUtils.getShortClassName(Class<?>)` calls `getShortClassName(String)` with the class name as a string representation, which is typically the fully qualified name including array encoding. 

The `getShortClassName(String)` method currently extracts the substring after the last package separator (dot) but does not handle Java array type signatures properly. The comment on line 192 indicates there was an intention or placeholder to "Handle array encoding" and "Strip Object type encoding", but that logic is missing or not implemented. 

Java arrays have class names with special encodings, e.g. "[Ljava.lang.String;" for `String[]`. The current method simply takes the substring after the last dot and returns it. Because array class names include '[' at the beginning and a trailing ';' after the class name, these characters are not stripped, causing the returned short name to include unwanted characters such as the semicolon at the end, e.g. "String;". This matches the symptom in the bug report and failing test.

No handling for these array type name formats like unwrapping the array notation to produce a clean "String[]" is present in the current implementation, which leads to incorrect short class names for array types.

The likely cause of the bug is the incomplete or missing implementation to decode and correctly format array class names into their expected human-readable form in the `getShortClassName(String)` method.

Recent bug reports are unrelated to this issue and do not provide relevant insights.

Next, I can suggest the specific method that must be fixed to properly handle array class names.

Class/method to fix:
- org.apache.commons.lang.ClassUtils.getShortClassName(String)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
